Mr. Nitin Panwad, after which the management will open the forum for the Q&A session.

call may be forward-looking in nature and must be viewed in conjunction with the risks and

Sunil Agrawal: 
Thank you, Deepali. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining Vaibhav Global 
Limited's Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. I hope you have had the opportunity to 
review our results and investor presentation. Q2 was a quarter of transition and an important 
one. 
 
During the quarter, we completed 2 of the major operational projects. The migration of all our 
retail websites to Shopify Enterprise and the consolidation of our U.K. 4 different sites into 
single headquarters. Both are now behind us. They came at a near-term cost, which I will 
quantify, but they leave us with a simpler and more scalable business as we enter the seasonally 
important second half. 
 
What the new platform unlocks. I want to spend a moment explaining why we made the move 
to Shopify as the cost of these transitions are visible in current quarter, while the benefits will 
build over coming quarters. This was a conscious and considered strategic decision, keeping our 
long-term commitments and business objectives in mind. 
 
First, we now operate one platform across all our 6 retail brands. Our feature built once can be 
deployed in every market so we can move faster and at lower cost. Second, we have a unified

view of our customers across TV and digital, built on first-party data, which supports better 
personalization, higher repeat purchase and greater customer lifetime value. 
 
Third, the platform integrates natively with modern marketing technology and AI tools, which 
are appealing our advertising creatives, product descriptions and SEO content. Fourth, we expect 
a lower long-term technology cost than our earlier legacy platform. 
 
And finally, we can launch new brands, categories and geographies far more quickly. Let me be 
specific about the cost. When we spoke in August, we flagged some initial disruption as we 
moved off our legacy platform. The stabilization took longer than we had planned and affected 
traffic and conversions across all the 4 business units where we made this transition. 
 
Based on our internal assessment, the revenue impact in the quarter was approximately USD2.8 
million or around 2.8 percentage point of growth. This is also why digital share of B2C revenue 
moved down by around 3 percentage points compared with Q1. At the same time, in the U.K., 
we consolidated 4 warehouses and 2 studios into a single site. This temporarily took some 
inventory offline and had a modest impact on sales. 
 
What gives me confidence is how the underlying model performed in the tougher consumer 
environment. Retail volumes grew approximately 2%, driven by strong demand for our lower 
price point items. Customers are clearly seeking value. And because we design, source and 
manufacture much of what we sell, we can meet the demand and still expand the gross margin, 
which rose by close to 197 basis points this quarter. 
 
Revenue for the quarter grew 7% to INR938.4 crores with reported growth supported by a 
weaker rupee. Gross margin expanded by approximately 197 basis points to 65.5%. EBITDA 
was INR76.2 crores, down 13.5%, with a margin of 8.1% compared to 10% in Q2 last year. 
 
Our EBITDA could have been 2% higher, whereas the same was not accounted due to reduction 
of 100 basis points related to Shopify and U.K. warehouse migration and 30 basis points related 
to lower forex gain than last year and remaining due to higher volume growth resulting in higher 
shipping costs. 
 
For the first half, revenue grew 9.7% to INR1,855.4 crores. EBITDA rose 9.6% to INR178.3 
crores. The decline in quarterly profitability is mainly related to operating leverage in the U.S. 
and U.K. due to transition. We see these pressures as transitional. 
 
Sustainability and community impact remain embedded in our business model. VGL's ICRA 
combined ESG rating further improved to 75 from 72, 2 years ago, rated strong. Through our 
Your purchase feeds program, more than 119 million meals have been distributed to date, and 
we now serve approximately 56,000 meals every school day, up from 55,000 a year ago. 
 
We remain committed to our long-term ambition of 1 million meals per school day by FY 2040. 
The Board has declared a second interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity share, following the first 
interim dividend of INR1.5 per share in Q1 FY27. Our capital allocation approach continues to 
balance investment in growth, shareholder returns and balance sheet strength.

Outlook. On guidance, we want to be transparent and prudent. We are taking into account the 
migration impact in Q2, the U.K. consolidation, a weaker U.K. consumer and the upcoming U.S. 
midterm election. We now expect revenue growth of 7% to 9% in FY27 compared with our 
earlier guidance of 9% to 11%. 
 
While the ongoing platform transition has impacted near-term growth, we believe the 
investments and structural improvements underway will strengthen our digital business and 
create a more scalable foundation for sustainable growth. 
 
Looking ahead, we remain confident in our ability to return to 9% to 11% revenue growth in 
FY28, supported by our new digital-first platforms, enhanced marketing capabilities and greater 
operational efficiency. 
 
The transition to Shopify is a strategic step towards achieving this objective, positioning us to 
accelerate digital growth and drive sustainable profitable growth over the medium term. We 
expect FY27 EBITDA margin to be broadly in line with FY26 compared with our earlier 
expectation of 50 to 100 basis points of expansion. 
 
We believe this is the right call, and it does not change our medium-term view. The unified 
digital platform, proprietary brands, lab-grown diamonds and our vertically integrated operating 
model positions us for stronger customer engagement, better quality of growth and improved 
profitability. 
 
With that, I hand over to Nitin to take you through financial performance in more detail. Over 
to you, Nitin. 
Nitin Panwad: 
Thank you, Sunil, and good afternoon, everyone. I will take you through the financial and 
operating performance for the second quarter and first half of FY27. Revenue from operations 
grew 7% year-over-year to INR938 crores. Retail revenue grew 5.3% to INR867.5 crores and 
B2B revenue grew 32% to INR70.9 crores. 
 
Currency was significant tailwind. The rupee weakened approximately 9% against the U.S. 
dollar,. In U.S., revenue grew 4.3% to INR500 crores in rupee terms and declined 4.1% in 
constant currency. The shift towards value is clearest here. 
 
Unit rose 4.8%, while the average selling price was 8.4% lower as consumer moved to lower 
price point. Digital share was 44% of revenue and EBITDA margin was 5.7%, reflecting sales 
deleverage of our investment in connected TV, OTT, app-based guiding to extend our reach 
beyond linear TV. Our vertical integrated supply chain continues to help us mitigate the impact 
of tariff. For the first half, U.S. EBITDA grew 24.9% to INR86.6 crores with margin up 102 
basis points to 8.4%.  
                                                The U.K. had a most challenging quarter. Revenues grew 2.3% to INR257.2 crores in rupee 
terms, but declined 7% in constant currency. 
 
Three factors were at play, the platform migration, temporary product unavailability during the 
warehouse consolidation and a noticeably weaker consumer sentiments. U.K. inflation rose to

digital to return to its earlier growth trajectory, and we continue to work towards our target of 
digital share at 50% of B2C revenue by Q4 FY27. 
 
Lifestyle products contributed approximately 40% of B2C revenue, and we continue to work 
towards a medium-term objective of 50% share. Budget accounted approximately 35% of retail 
revenue. It remains an important affordability tool supporting conversion and accessibility, 
particularly for higher value purchases. 
 
In-house brands contributed 57% of B2C revenue and the lab-grown diamond share rose to 12% 
of total retail revenue from about 10% a year back, strengthening our differentiation and pricing. 
Under our 4R framework, we reached more than 127 million households with approximately 
687,000 unique customers on a trailing 12-month basis and 360,000 new customers acquired 
over trailing 12 months, 38% retention and an average of 23 pieces per customer buying per 
year. 
 
Group's gross margin improved by approximately 197 basis points to 65.5% from 63.5% in Q2 
FY26, supported by vertical integration, in-house brands and growing share of lab-grown 
diamonds. The first half gross margin was 65.5% compared to 63.6% in H1 FY26. EBITDA was 
INR76.2 crores with a margin of 8.1%, lower by 193 basis points year-over-year despite the 
gross margin expansion. 
 
The movement reflects the retail sales deleverage during the transition. The first half revenue 
increased 9.7% to INR1,855 crores. EBITDA increased 9.6% to INR178 crores with a margin 
of 9.6% and profit after tax increased to INR98.1 crores with a growth of 15.2% year-over-year. 
 
Moving to our balance sheet. As of September 30, 2026, our net cash stood at INR186 crores 
compared to INR279 crores of March '26. This reduction is mainly related to seasonal inventory 
buildup and capex related to U.K. warehouse migration of INR36 crores. The ROCE stood at 
22% and ROE at 18%. 
 
As Sunil mentioned, the Board has declared the second interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity 
share. Our capital allocation remained disciplined with priority given to digital growth,

our platform migration and U.K. consolidation, expanded gross margin by 197 basis points, grew 
volume in difficult consumer environment, delivered strong B2B growth and continued to strong 
constant currency growth in Europe.

operations.
